lessons.title: Do not consume unjustly
lessons.intro: The base rule for earning and trading from 4:29 and 2:188, and an audit of your own income.

steps.title: Whose money is it?
body: Money passes from hand to hand all day: wages, prices, tips, loans, gifts. Islam asks one question about every transfer: is it fair?
This lesson is about 4:29 and 2:188, the two ayat that set the base rule for earning and trading, and a short audit you can use on your own income.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Not unjustly, but by consent
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah says: do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly, but only through lawful business by mutual consent. The rule has two halves: not unjust, and lawful trade by mutual consent. Read the meaning under the ayah.

steps.title: Hear the ayah
steps.note: Listen, then say it after the reciter in the pause.

steps.title: Not through bribery
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: A second ayah: do not consume one another’s wealth unjustly, and do not pass it to the rulers so that they will help you take part of other people’s wealth in sin, while you know. This is the ayah about bribery.

steps.title: Consent is not enough by itself
body: The ayah of 4:29 says the trade must be by mutual consent, and it also says lawful business. So consent is necessary, but a deal can still be wrong if the thing traded is forbidden, if one side is deceived, or if one side is forced by need into unfair terms.
Teachers often summarise it in three questions: Did both sides agree freely? Is the thing itself lawful? Was everything described honestly? The summary is a teaching aid, not a quotation.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The three-question summary of a valid deal is a teaching aid. Please confirm that it is acceptable as stated.

steps.title: Truth brings blessing
body: Hakim ibn Hizam reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: the buyer and seller have the choice as long as they have not parted. If they both speak the truth and make clear the defects, their transaction is blessed. If they lie and conceal, the blessing of the transaction is lost (Bukhari 2079).
So the Prophet ﷺ ties the blessing (barakah) of a deal to honesty about the goods. The amount may be the same, but the barakah is different.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Ways money is taken unjustly
steps.intro: These are common forms. The list is a teaching summary, not a full legal list.
steps.agree: All of these are forms of consuming wealth unjustly.

rows.name: Deception
rows.text: Hiding a fault, giving a false description, or lying about the price.

rows.name: Bribery
rows.text: Paying someone in power so that they help you take what is not yours (2:188).

rows.name: Taking by pressure
rows.text: Using someone’s need or fear to force an unfair price.

rows.name: Taking what is not earned
rows.text: Theft, fraud, and cheating an employer or a customer.

steps.closing: Ask of each: would I accept this if I were the other person?
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The list of unjust forms is a teaching summary. Please confirm.

steps.title: Audit one source of income
steps.intro: Do this once, with a pen. It takes ten minutes.

steps.text: Write down one source of money.
steps.detail: A job, a side business, an allowance, or a loan.

steps.text: Ask: how does the money come to me?
steps.detail: Describe it in plain words.

steps.text: Ask: is anyone deceived or harmed?
steps.detail: The customer, the employer, the public?

steps.text: Ask: is the work or product lawful?
steps.detail: If you are not sure, write the question down.

steps.text: Ask: do I feel uneasy about it?
steps.detail: If yes, take it to someone who knows.

steps.text: Ask a scholar about anything grey.
steps.detail: Bring the details. Do not hide parts.

mistakes: Assuming it is fine because everyone does it.
Giving only half the details when you ask.
Waiting until the end of the year.
steps.label: [Reflection]

lessons.title: The birds leave hungry
lessons.intro: Trust in Allah with effort, from the hadith of the birds and the ayat of provision.

steps.title: Plan, then let go
body: Money worry keeps people awake. Some give up and wait for provision; others grab at everything in fear. Neither is what the Prophet ﷺ described.
In this lesson, a hadith about birds shows trust in Allah (tawakkul) with action. You will read two ayat on provision and learn a du’a for what Allah has made lawful.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: The bird
body: Umar reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: if you were to rely upon Allah as He should be relied upon, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds. They go out in the morning empty and return full (Tirmidhi 2344 (graded sahih by al-Albani)).
Look at what the bird does. It goes out. It does not wait in the nest. Trust in Allah and effort go together.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Provision is with Allah
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah says there is no creature on earth whose provision is not upon Allah. He knows where it lives and where it is stored. All is in a clear register.

steps.title: Walk and eat of His provision
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah made the earth tame for you: walk in its paths and eat of His provision. The ayah gives the movement and the source together.

steps.title: A way out
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah says that whoever fears Him, He makes for him a way out, and provides for him from where he does not expect. Whoever relies upon Allah, He is sufficient for him.

steps.title: Trust and effort
steps.intro: A short comparison of three ways of facing a need.
steps.agree: The bird in the hadith goes out, and Allah provides.

rows.name: Giving up
rows.text: Sitting back and saying Allah will provide, without working. This is not what the bird does.

rows.name: Panic
rows.text: Chasing everything out of fear, and breaking rules to get ahead.

rows.name: Tawakkul
rows.text: Do what is in your hands, honestly, and leave the result to Allah.

steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The three-way comparison is a teaching summary based on the hadith of the bird. Please confirm.

steps.title: A du’a for what is lawful
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Ali reported that the Prophet ﷺ taught this du’a, and said that if a person had a debt like a mountain, Allah would help pay it. The words ask Allah to be enough with His lawful instead of the unlawful, and to make you need nobody but Him. There is no recording of this du’a in the app yet. Source: Tirmidhi 3563 (graded hasan by al-Albani).

steps.title: Plan, then release
steps.intro: Use this for one worry about money this week.

steps.detail: In one sentence. For example: I may not have enough for rent.

steps.text: Write what is in your hands.
steps.detail: Work, a budget, a call to the landlord, a request for help.
A small step.
For lawful provision (Tirmidhi 3563 (graded hasan by al-Albani)).
Do not break a rule to get ahead.

mistakes: Doing nothing and calling it trust.
Breaking the rules because of fear.
Checking the same account every hour.

lessons.title: The honest measure
lessons.intro: The warning of Surah Al-Mutaffifin, the story of Shu’ayb, and the hadith of the wet grain.

steps.title: Exactly one kilo
body: A scale that reads a little light. A deadline that is a little loose. A promise made to get the sale. Small cheats feel harmless. The Qur’an does not treat them that way.
In this lesson you will read the surah that opens with a warning to those who give less than they owe, the story of Shu’ayb, and a hadith about hiding a fault in the goods.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Woe to those who give less
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Surah Al-Mutaffifin opens with a warning. Woe to those who give less than due: when they take a measure from people they take in full, but when they give by measure or weight to them, they cause loss.

steps.title: Hear the opening
steps.note: Listen to the first ayah of the surah.

steps.title: Shu’ayb’s people
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: The prophet Shu’ayb told his people not to decrease the measure and the scale, and to give full measure and weight in justice, and not to deprive people of their due. The Qur’an remembers him for this message.

steps.title: The wet grain
body: Abu Huraira reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ passed a heap of grain. He put his hand in and his fingers touched wetness. He asked the owner: what is this? The owner said: the rain fell on it. The Prophet ﷺ said: why did you not put it on top so that people could see it? Whoever deceives is not of me (Muslim 102).
The seller had not said anything false. He just let the buyer see only the dry part. The Prophet ﷺ still called it deception.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Not of us
body: In another report he said: whoever acts dishonestly towards us is not of us (Muslim 101). Scholars take this wording as a strong warning. Many explain that it means that this person is not following the Prophet’s way, and not that he has left Islam.
The lesson here is simple: honesty in a deal is part of following the Prophet ﷺ.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The explanation that not of us is a strong warning and not a declaration of leaving Islam is the common scholarly reading. Please confirm.

steps.title: Small cheats
body: It is easy to think that 83:1-3 is only for market traders with scales. Teachers apply it more widely: to a worker who gives less time than paid for, a student who gives less effort than a degree requires, and a person who takes full rights and gives less than his due. This wider use is an application of the principle, not the wording of the ayah.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Applying 83:1-3 to workers and students is a common application; please confirm.

steps.title: Make one measure exact

steps.detail: A scale, a deadline, a promise, a timesheet, a delivery time.
Is it exact, or a little in your favour?
Change the price, the time, or the promise.
Tell the other person what it is. Do not hide the wet part.
See how it feels.

mistakes: Thinking a small amount does not count.
Fixing it only when you are watched.
Making an honest promise you cannot keep.

lessons.title: Honest work over easy wealth
lessons.intro: Earning with your own hands, not asking when you can work, and the barakah of a generous soul.

steps.title: Which money feels best?
body: A first wage from a hard day. A gift from a relative. A lucky win. Most people say the first feels different. This lesson looks at why.
It uses three hadith about earning with your own hands and asking from people, and one about taking wealth with a generous soul or with greed.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: The best meal
body: Al-Miqdam reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: no one has eaten a better meal than one he has earned by working with his own hands. The prophet of Allah, Dawud, used to eat from the earnings of his hands (Bukhari 2072).
The Prophet ﷺ did not say that hand-work is the only honest work. He was praising earning, not complaining about other jobs.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Rather than ask
body: Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: it is better for one of you to take his rope, bring a bundle of wood on his back and sell it, than to go to someone and ask them, whether they give him or refuse (Bukhari 1470).
This is not a rule against taking help when you are in real need. The Prophet ﷺ also taught that the poor have a right in zakat. The hadith is about not turning to asking when you can work.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Pious, independent, hidden
body: Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: Allah loves the servant who is God-conscious, free from want, and hidden (Muslim 2965).
Free from want does not mean rich. It means a heart that does not depend on people. Hidden means not seeking attention.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A generous soul
body: Hakim ibn Hizam reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: this wealth is like sweet fresh fruit. Whoever takes it without greed will be blessed in it, and whoever takes it with greed will not be blessed in it, like one who eats and is never satisfied. The upper hand is better than the lower hand (Bukhari 1472).
So barakah is not decided by the amount. It depends on how the wealth is taken and how the heart is.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Work, then remember Allah
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: After Friday prayer Allah says: when the prayer is finished, spread out in the land, seek from the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often so that you may succeed. Work and remembrance are joined.

lessons.title: What riba actually is
lessons.intro: What the Qur’an and hadith say about riba, the two kinds, and a way to check one product.

steps.title: A loan is a trust
body: You lend a friend some money. A month later he gives you back a little more, saying thank you. Is that fine? What if you had asked for the extra at the start?

This lesson explains what riba is in the Qur’an, the two hadith that say how seriously it is taken, and the two kinds that scholars talk about. It does not tell you what to do with your own bank; the next lessons come to that.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Trade is permitted, interest is forbidden
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah describes those who consume interest and says that they say trade is just like interest, but Allah has permitted trade and forbidden interest. Whoever receives an admonition and desists may keep what is past, and his affair is with Allah. Read the meaning.

steps.title: Allah destroys interest
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah destroys interest and gives increase for charities. Money that seems to grow through interest does not grow with Allah, and money given in charity does (also 30:39).

steps.title: Doubled and multiplied
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.note: Allah says: do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied, but fear Allah so that you may be successful. Scholars note that this describes the practice of the time and do not take it to mean that only doubled interest is forbidden.
steps.review: The note that scholars do not take doubled and multiplied as a limit on the prohibition is the common reading; please confirm.

steps.title: A strong warning
body: Jabir reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ cursed the one who takes interest, the one who pays it, the one who records it, and the two witnesses, and said: they are all the same (Muslim 1598).
The warning covers the whole chain. That is why scholars say riba is not only a matter for the lender.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Two kinds scholars discuss
steps.intro: The hadith in Muslim 1584 lists six items, and the schools differ on what else it covers.
steps.agree: All agree that stipulated increase on a loan is forbidden.

rows.name: Riba of delay (nasi’a)
rows.text: An increase that is stipulated in return for waiting or for more time on a loan. This is the kind most people mean by interest.

rows.name: Riba of excess (fadl)
rows.text: An excess when trading the same kind of item for itself, for example gold for more gold, hand to hand. Muslim 1584 mentions gold, silver, wheat, barley, dates and salt, like for like, hand to hand.

rows.name: Where scholars differ
rows.text: The schools differ on what else belongs with the six items named, because they explain the reason differently: Hanafis by weight or volume of the same kind, Shafi’is by being a currency or a food, Malikis by staple foods that can be stored, Hanbalis by weight or volume.

steps.closing: If you are not sure whether a product contains riba, ask a qualified scholar.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Please confirm the definitions of nasi’a and fadl and the one-line summary of each school’s reason (illa) for the six items.

lessons.title: Interest in everyday life
lessons.intro: What scholars say about cards, plans, loans and savings interest, and how to start an exit.

steps.title: It is in the small print
body: A card balance. A buy-now-pay-later plan. A student loan. A car on finance. A savings account that pays interest. The word riba is old, but the products are new.
This lesson sets out what scholars say about these everyday cases and where they disagree. It does not give you a verdict on your own contract. It helps you ask a good question.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: What most scholars say
body: Large fiqh bodies, including the Islamic Fiqh Academy of the OIC and the Fiqh Council of the Muslim World League, have stated that conventional bank interest is riba. Many scholars hold the same view. A small number of modern scholars have argued the other way, mostly on the basis of how banks and money work today, and the majority have not accepted it.
The Qur’an itself says that Allah destroys interest (2:276) and that a stipulated increase on a loan is the thing forbidden (2:278-279).
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Please confirm the statement about the OIC Fiqh Academy and the Muslim World League Fiqh Council, and the minority view.

steps.title: Common cases and common questions
steps.intro: These are the questions people ask most. The answers are not settled by this lesson.
steps.agree: Most scholars agree that stipulated increase on a loan is forbidden.

rows.name: A card balance
rows.text: Interest on a balance you carry is stipulated increase on a loan. Paying the balance in full before interest applies is a different thing. Ask about fees.

rows.name: Buy now, pay later
rows.text: Some plans have no fee if paid on time and a penalty if late. Scholars discuss late penalties. Ask about your plan.

rows.name: Student loan or car finance
rows.text: These are loans with interest. Some Islamic finance products exist. Scholars debate how closely they follow the rules.

rows.name: Interest on savings
rows.text: Many scholars say a Muslim should not keep interest paid on savings, and should give that part to charity without expecting reward. Others hold a different view. Ask a scholar.

steps.closing: Ask a qualified scholar about your own contract.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Please confirm each case summary, especially the advice about interest on savings and about late penalties.

steps.title: Why it is taken seriously
body: The Prophet ﷺ cursed the taker, the payer, the recorder and the two witnesses (Muslim 1598). And in Bukhari 2086, Awn ibn Abi Juhayfa reported that the Prophet ﷺ forbade giving and receiving riba, among other things. Because the warning is so strong, the right response is care, not panic.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: What the lesson does not say
body: The old version of this lesson said that the world economy runs on riba. That is a claim about economics that this app cannot source, so it has been removed. The lesson only says what the sources and the scholars say.
It also does not say that anyone who uses a card is a sinner. It asks you to learn, to ask, and to move step by step.

lessons.title: Leaving riba with dignity
lessons.intro: The verses of giving up riba, ease for those in hardship, and the first steps out.

steps.title: A way out with dignity
body: If you are in debt with interest, shame and fear are common. The Qur’an speaks to this situation with firmness and with mercy.

This lesson reads the verses that tell believers to give up what remains of riba, what they may keep, and how a lender is to treat someone in hardship. It adds a prophetic example of repaying well, and one du’a.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Give up what remains
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah tells the believers to fear Him and give up what remains of interest, if they are believers. If they do not, they are informed of a war from Allah and His Messenger. But if they repent, they may have their principal: they do no wrong and are not wronged.

steps.title: Hear the ayah
steps.note: Listen to the ayah of repentance and the principal.

steps.title: Ease for the one in hardship
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: If someone is in hardship, there should be postponement until ease. To give it up as charity is better, if you only knew. This ayah is for the lender: do not press someone who cannot pay.

steps.title: What war means here
body: The Qur’an uses the language of war from Allah and His Messenger for those who refuse to give up what remains of riba. It is a very strong sentence. Notice what comes right after: but if you repent, you may have your principal. The door of repentance is in the same ayah.
The lesson should not be used to frighten someone who is trying. It shows how serious the matter is and how open the way back is.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Please confirm the explanation of the war ayah and that repentance is in the same ayah.

steps.title: Repay well
body: Abu Huraira reported that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ to demand a camel owed to him. The Prophet ﷺ told his companions to give him one. They found only an older camel. He said: give it to him, for the best among you is the one who repays in the best manner (Bukhari 2392).
Repaying a debt with grace is a sunnah. It is a good habit to keep when you are leaving a bad one.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: A du’a for debt and worry
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Anas reported that the Prophet ﷺ used to make this du’a (Bukhari 6369): he sought refuge in Allah from worry and grief, from weakness and laziness, from cowardice and stinginess, and from the weight of debt and from being overpowered by men. There is no recording of it in the app yet.

steps.title: Home loans: where scholars differ
steps.intro: This is one of the most disputed practical questions. The lesson only reports the positions.
steps.agree: Everyone agrees on the seriousness of interest.

rows.name: The majority position
rows.text: Many scholars and fiqh bodies say a conventional mortgage is a loan with interest and is not allowed, and recommend Islamic home finance or saving.

rows.name: A minority position
rows.text: Some contemporary councils, such as the European Council for Fatwa and Research, have permitted a home loan for Muslims living as minorities under strict conditions of need. Others disagree with them.

rows.name: What to do
rows.text: Do not decide alone from a website. Ask a qualified scholar about your exact situation.

steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Please confirm the summary of positions on mortgages and the reference to the European Council for Fatwa and Research.

lessons.title: Zakat on savings
lessons.intro: Who pays zakat, the nisab and the year, how to work out 2.5 percent, and who receives it.

steps.title: The part that is not yours
body: Some of the money in your account was never really yours to keep. Zakat is the share that belongs to others. Many people give it but are unsure how to work it out.
This lesson explains who must give zakat, what the nisab and the year mean, how to work out 2.5 percent, and who receives it. Scholars differ on some calculation details, so those are flagged.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Take from their wealth
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah tells His Messenger to take from their wealth a charity by which he purifies them and causes them increase, and to pray for them. Zakat is a purification of wealth and of the giver.

steps.title: From the wealthy to the poor
body: Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet ﷺ sent Mu’adh to Yemen and told him to teach the people that Allah has made zakat obligatory on their property, to be taken from the wealthy among them and given to the poor among them (Bukhari 1395).
This tells you two things: zakat is a duty, not a favour, and it goes to people who need it.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The nisab
body: The Prophet ﷺ said that there is no zakat on less than five uqiyas of silver (Bukhari 1405). Scholars take the minimum amount from reports like this, and it is called the nisab. For silver this is 200 dirhams, which many calculate as about 595 grams. Gold has a nisab of 20 dinars, commonly calculated as about 85 grams.
The exact gram values are conventions used by scholars and councils and are not stated in the hadith. Check a current figure from a trusted authority before calculating.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Please confirm the gram values (595 g silver, 85 g gold) and the statement that the gold nisab is derived from other reports.

steps.title: Gold or silver for cash?
steps.intro: Cash was not around in the Prophet’s time in its present form, so scholars differ on which nisab to use for savings.
steps.agree: All agree that zakat is due on wealth above the nisab.

rows.name: Silver nisab
rows.text: It is lower in value today, so more people would owe zakat. Some scholars, among them many Hanafis, prefer whichever benefits the poor, which is usually silver.

rows.name: Gold nisab
rows.text: It is higher in value today. Others, including many scholars of the other schools, use gold for savings in cash.

rows.name: Your next step
rows.text: Choose the view of a scholar you follow, and keep to it. If in doubt, use the lower nisab, which is the cautious choice.

steps.closing: Follow a scholar you trust, and be cautious.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: Please confirm the summary of the schools on which nisab applies to cash, and the cautious-choice suggestion.

steps.title: The year and the rate
body: Zakat is due once a year, on wealth that you have held at or above the nisab for a full lunar year. This one-year condition is held by the schools, based on reports of the Companions. The rate for cash and silver is 2.5 percent, which is one-fortieth. Abu Bakr’s letter, reported in Bukhari 1454, gives one-fortieth for silver.
So to work it out: add up the zakatable wealth you have on your zakat date, subtract short-term debts you owe, and take 2.5 percent if what is left is above the nisab.
steps.label: [Interpretive]
steps.review: The year condition is stated on the authority of the schools and the Companions; I did not verify the individual reports. Please confirm, and confirm the debt-subtraction step.

steps.title: Who receives zakat
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah names the eight groups: the poor, the needy, those who collect it, those whose hearts are to be reconciled, freeing captives, those in debt, in the cause of Allah, and the traveller in need. It is an obligation from Allah.

steps.title: Work out your zakat
steps.intro: This is an outline. Use your own scholar’s rules for details.

steps.detail: The same date each year, for example the first of Ramadan.

steps.text: Add up what you have on that date.
steps.detail: Cash, savings, gold and silver you hold as savings, money owed to you that you expect back.
Many scholars allow this. Ask about long-term loans.
If it is below, nothing is due. If above, continue.

steps.text: Take 2.5 percent of what is left.
steps.detail: Multiply by 0.025.

steps.text: Pay it to those who qualify.
steps.detail: Choose from the groups in 9:60, directly or through a trusted charity.

mistakes: Counting your house and car you live in.
Giving it to people who are not in the groups.
Waiting for the date to pass.

lessons.title: Debt and the door
lessons.intro: The promise for one who intends to repay, the seriousness of debt, and a plan to carry it.

steps.title: A weight with a door
body: Debt can be a heavy thing to carry. It is also not a shame to be in debt if you are working to repay. The Prophet ﷺ spoke about it often, with both warning and hope.
This lesson has a promise for the one who borrows intending to repay, a warning, a story about a funeral prayer, a du’a, and practical steps.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Intending to repay
body: Abu Huraira reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: whoever takes people’s money intending to repay it, Allah will repay it for him; and whoever takes it intending to destroy it, Allah will destroy him (Bukhari 2387).
The intention is part of the borrowing. A person who borrows with the real intention to repay, and works at it, is promised help from Allah.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: But it is serious
body: Amr ibn al-As reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: all the sins of a martyr are forgiven except debt (Muslim 1886). This shows how seriously the rights of people are taken: they are not wiped out like other things.
So debt is not a reason for despair. It is a reason to take repaying seriously, to write it down, and to tell the family so that it is not lost.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The funeral prayer
body: Salama ibn al-Akwa reported that a dead man was brought to the Prophet ﷺ to lead the funeral prayer. He asked: is he in debt? They said: yes, three dinars, and he left nothing. He said: then pray for your companion. Abu Qatada said: O Messenger of Allah, I will pay his debt. So the Prophet ﷺ led the prayer (Bukhari 2289).
The story is not about being harsh. It teaches that debts belong to the living and the dead alike, and that those who help repay carry a real kindness.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Ease for the debtor
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah tells the lender to give time to someone in hardship, and says that giving it up as charity is better. If you are the one in debt, this is a right to ask for time; if you are the lender, it is a duty.

steps.title: Write it down
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: The longest ayah of the Qur’an is about debts with a fixed term: write them down, let a scribe write between you in justice, and call witnesses. A written record protects both sides. Read the meaning of the first lines.

steps.title: The du’a of the indebted
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: From the du’a of Bukhari 6369: I seek refuge in You from the weight of debt and from being overpowered by men. There is no recording of it in the app yet.

steps.title: When you repay
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: When the Prophet ﷺ repaid a loan, he said: may Allah bless your family and your wealth; the reward of a loan is praise and repayment (Nasa’i 4683 (graded sahih by al-Albani)). You can say this to a lender when you repay. There is no recording of it in the app yet.

Muslim 1886 shows debts must not be lost.

steps.detail: A fixed monthly amount.
And ask Allah to pay it for you (Bukhari 2387).

steps.text: When you repay, thank the lender.
steps.detail: Say the words above.

Borrowing again with no intention to repay.

lessons.title: Barakah, not just more
lessons.intro: What the Prophet ﷺ said about barakah, honest work, early hours and rest.

steps.title: More is not the same as enough
body: Some people have a lot and are always short. Others have little and are fine. The Prophet ﷺ had a word for this: barakah, the blessing that makes a little enough.
This lesson follows what the Prophet ﷺ said about barakah in wealth, in time, and in rest. It does not claim that prayer cures burnout. It says what the sources say and when to ask for help.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Sweet fruit, taken with a generous soul
body: Hakim ibn Hizam reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: this wealth is like sweet fresh fruit. Whoever takes it without greed will be blessed in it, and whoever takes it with greed will not be blessed in it, like one who eats and is never satisfied (Bukhari 1472).
Barakah here is not about the amount. It is about being satisfied. The person who is never satisfied does not feel blessed even with more.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Honesty in a deal
body: In Bukhari 2079 the Prophet ﷺ said that if buyer and seller speak the truth and make clear the defects, they will be blessed in the deal; if they lie and hide, the blessing of the deal is lost.
So honest work protects barakah.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Blessings from the heavens and earth
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: Allah says that if the people of the towns had believed and feared Allah, He would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth. Barakah is linked to faith and taqwa.

steps.title: Blessing in the early hours
body: Sakhr al-Ghamidi reported that the Prophet ﷺ said: O Allah, bless my community in what they do early in the day. When he sent an army, he sent it at the beginning of the day. Sakhr was a trader who sent his goods early in the morning, and he became rich (Tirmidhi 1212 (graded sahih by al-Albani)).
This is practical: the early hours are a time of barakah for work.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: The du’a for early blessing
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: You can say this du’a at the start of the day. It asks Allah to bless the community in its early hours. There is no recording of it in the app yet. Source: Tirmidhi 1212 (graded sahih by al-Albani).

steps.title: Your body has a right
body: Abu Juhaifa reported that Salman visited his brother Abu al-Darda and found him fasting by day and praying by night. Salman told him: your Lord has a right on you, your soul has a right on you, and your family has a right on you, so give each its right. When Abu al-Darda told the Prophet ﷺ, he said: Salman has spoken the truth (Bukhari 1968).
The Prophet ﷺ did not praise exhausting yourself, even in worship. Rest and family are rights.
steps.label: [Established]

steps.title: Work, then remember
steps.label: [Established]
steps.note: After the prayer, spread out in the land, seek Allah’s bounty, and remember Allah often. Prayer and work take turns through the day.

steps.title: What this does not say
body: The old lesson claimed that the cure for burnout is barakah, and that the believer sleeps differently. This lesson does not claim that. Burnout and anxiety can have physical and mental causes. Faith helps many people, but if you feel exhausted, hopeless or cannot function, talk to a doctor or counsellor as well as to a scholar. Seeking treatment is not a lack of trust. The Prophet ﷺ taught tawakkul together with action.
steps.label: [Reflection]

steps.title: Protect one prayer like a meeting

steps.detail: The one that gets squeezed out most.
Treat it as fixed.

steps.text: Tell the people who need to know.
steps.detail: A colleague, a teacher, family.
Phone away.
See what changes.

mistakes: Praying at the end of the day for every prayer.
Skipping it when busy.
Using it as a cure for everything.
steps.label: [Reflection]

items.scenario: Reem is exhausted and cannot sleep. Someone tells her barakah will fix it.

steps.prompt: Put the steps in order.

items.text: Tell the people who need to know

steps.prompt: Match each text to its message. Tap one on the left, then its meaning on the right.

right.text: Wealth taken without greed is blessed
Honest deals are blessed
Blessings follow faith and taqwa
Blessing in the early hours
Your body and family have a right

items.q: Does the lesson say barakah cures burnout?

options.reteach: The lesson does not claim that.

options.text: No. It says seek a doctor or counsellor as well

items.q: What does Tirmidhi 1212 (graded sahih by al-Albani) say about early hours?

options.text: The Prophet ﷺ asked Allah to bless the community in what it does early in the day

items.q: What is barakah in Bukhari 1472?
What does 62:10 join?

options.text: Seeking Allah’s bounty and remembering Allah often
